newsitem.title: USA: Toy Biz tentatively agrees to acquire Marvel.
newsitem.headline: Toy Biz tentatively agrees to acquire Marvel.

text.p: Financier Ronald Perelman and bankers including Chase Manhattan have reached a deal to sell Marvel Entertainment Group Inc.'s comic book and entertainment operations to Toy Biz Inc., controlled by Isaac Perlmutter, Marvel said Monday.

In a series of plans that could bail out the struggling comic book publisher, Marvel's tentative agreement with Toy Biz also deals a blow to the competing bondholders' group headed by financier Carl Icahn.
Marvel said Toy Biz, which holds the licenses to some of Marvel's characters such as Spiderman and the Hulk, has agreed to buy its publishing and licensing businesses.
A group of dissident bondholders led by Icahn said it would oppose the latest plan.
Under the plan, Marvel's Fleer/SkyBox and Panini subsidiaries would be spun off to the creditor banks, and according to a source close to Toy Biz, would likely be sold.
Marvel filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December. Marvel could present the Toy Biz plan to the bankruptcy court this week.

Earlier in April, Perlmutter, who owns 35 percent of Toy Biz, presented Marvel's bank lenders with an offer to buy the comic book company. The deal would flip the tables somewhat, because Marvel owns over 26 percent of Toy Biz.
Toy Biz gets a significant portion of its revenues from sales of products based on characters owned by Marvel.

Under the Perlmutter plan, Marvel's creditors would receive cash for about two-thirds of the approximately $725 million they are owed. The money would come from a new $250 million term loan plus cash received from selling Fleer and Panini.
Then, the remaining bank debt will be converted into a 5-year, $170 million note, which will be held by existing creditors, the Toy Biz source said.
Marvel's secured lenders would then hold a 28 percent stake in the merged Marvel/Toy Biz, in addition to Fleer/Skybox and Panini.

The new combined company will issue warrants to existing stock holders that would let them purchase 7.5 percent of the company when the company's valuation reaches $950 million, the Toy Biz source said.
Another 5 percent of the merged company would be avaliable for sale to warrant holders when the combined company's value reaches $1.1 billion.

A Marvel spokesman said Marvel and Toybiz officials were working to finalise details of the proposal. The final plan will be subject to approval by the bankruptcy court as well as the Marvel and Toybiz boards, he said.
Marvel's lead lender, Chase Manhattan, has approved the proposed plan, the company said.
Meanwhile, the dissident bondholder committee of Marvel Entertainment Group, led by Icahn, said it planned to oppose the Marvel/Toy Biz plan, a spokesman for the committee said.

The bondholder committee said it will appeal a court ruling preventing committee members from voting their Marvel shares to oust Marvel's board. Oral arguments on the appeal are scheduled for Thursday, a committee spokesman said.
"We will fight this plan vigorously with every legal remedy available under the bankruptcy laws," the spokesman said.
"Marvel's board is abdicating its responsiblity to their shareholders in favour of the banks and Toy Biz insiders with this proposed plan," said the spokesman.

A Marvel spokesman, asked to comment on the bondholder committee criticism, said, "Anybody is welcome to bid and make an offer for the company. If it is worth what the bondholders say it is worth, then Marvel will receive a bid to that effect and the bondholders will receive the recovery they want."

Last week, the bondholder committee purchased an undisclosed amount of the company's bank debt and said it was seeking to buy more, according to a statement filed by the group with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Sources familiar with the situation said the purchases may signify that Marvel bondholders are interested in obtaining a seat at the table in any negotiations between holders of bank debt and Marvel.
Stock of Marvel Entertainment was unchanged at $2.25 and Toy Biz was up 12.5 cents at $10.375, both in late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
